MIT Pinpoints the Location of Memories in Individual Neurons Through Optogenetics

Maybe I'm all wet (I don't think so BTW) but I believe the NSA and the CIA (and other foreign governments too) are very interested in erasing some hardwired memories... I have absolutely zero doubt, and I'm very concerned -- and you should be too.
The sooner it gets out in the open, the sooner we can develop countermeasures for it.
or use it as an advertising medium...
It would still be immensely difficult to determine which neuron holds which memory, and what cascading effect it might have to selectively remove one.

So, reading the actual paper (better summary with actual content here) or having some background understanding of neuroscience clarifies the sensationalized title and hopefully quells some of the "fears" it might induce. No one can read your memories using lasers - the scientists just temporarily shut off some memory forming circuits during a learning task (something that's easy to do in an animal model and has been done for a long time) and were able to reactivate those circuits later using optogenetics - a technique involving activating neurons with light (wiki here).

It's a cool and important paper, and it's interesting news, but it's more a paper on "MIT scientists are learning about how memories are encoded" and not on "MIT scientists can read your mind".
